Further, Section 66E of the Information Technology Act, 2000 deals with the transmission of photos of any personâs private area without his or her consent on social media, which is a criminal offence and the penalty is either three years in prison or a fine of not more than two lakh rupees, or both. On investigation, if the police find that the person is in any way violating the provisions of the Act, he can be booked for committing the crime under Section 66E of the Information Technology Act, 2000. Any person who feels their reputation has been damaged by defamatory statements or acts can sue for defamation under Section 356 of BNS, which replaced Section 499 of IPC. If a person is found guilty of criminal defamation, they can be sentenced to imprisonment for up to two years, a fine, or both under Section 500 of the IPC, replaced by Section 356(2) of the BNS. answer_ref: Dear Client,Domestic violence in India is covered under several laws, primarily under the Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act, 2005 (PWDVA), and the Indian Penal Code (IPC). Section 498A and Section 352 of the IPC address specific aspects of domestic violence.Understanding the Sections:Section 498A IPC:Objective: To protect married women from cruelty by their husbands and in-laws.Definition: It covers any willful conduct that is likely to drive a woman to suicide or cause grave injury to her life, limb, or health (whether mental or physical). It also includes harassment with the aim of coercing her or her relatives to meet any unlawful demand for property or valuable security.Punishment: Imprisonment for up to three years and a fine.Section 352 IPC:Objective: To address assault or use of criminal force otherwise than on grave provocation.Definition: It penalizes the act of assault or use of criminal force against any person without grave and sudden provocation by that person.Punishment: Imprisonment for up to three months, or a fine of up to five hundred rupees, or both.Determining the Applicability:Section 498A: If the case involves a married woman being subjected to cruelty by her husband or in-laws, particularly with respect to harassment for dowry or inflicting harm that could cause serious mental or physical trauma, then it falls under Section 498A.Section 352: If the situation involves an incident where assault or use of criminal force occurred without grave provocation but does not fit the specific criteria of cruelty in a matrimonial context as described in Section 498A, it might fall under Section 352.
answer_pred:
Section 498A of the Indian Penal Code deals with cruelty by a husband or his relatives towards a woman, which is a criminal offense, while Section 352 deals with assault or use of criminal force otherwise than on grave provocation. If the issue involves cruelty by a husband or his relatives, it falls under Section 498A, which is specifically related to domestic violence. Section 352, on the other hand, would apply to general assault cases not specifically related to domestic violence.

To address your situation, determine whether the allegations pertain to cruelty by a husband or relatives (498A) or general assault (352). If it is a 498A case, you may need to gather evidence of cruelty and file a complaint with the police. If it's a 352 case, evidence of the assault or use of force should be collected to support the complaint.

answer_ref: Dear Client,A person aggrieved by defamation has a right to proceed both in the civil Court as well as in the criminal Court. He can take either one or the other or both courses. Law does not debar him from enforcing civil and criminal rights at the same time. In India, defamation is categorized as either criminal or civil, and both types are covered by the Indian Penal Code (IPC) and the Code of Civil Procedure (CPC). In Civil Defamation, a person who is defamed can move the competent Court having pecuniary jurisdiction and seek damages in the form of monetary compensation. Under Section 19 of the Civil Procedure Code (CPC), a civil suit can be filed either where the Defendant resides or where the Defamatory statement was made/published. A defamation of a criminal nature has been codified under Sections 499 and 500 of the Indian Penal Code 1860 and to file a criminal suit under this Section, a person must have made an imputation about another person with either an intention, knowledge, or reason to believe that such an imputation will harm the reputation of the said person. Under criminal defamation, individuals can be charged with an offense punishable by imprisonment for two years or a fine. As per the Limitation Act, there is a limitation period of one year for filing a civil defamation suit and the limitation to file a criminal defamation complaint is 3 years from the period of knowledge of offense.
answer_pred: Yes, a defamation case can be filed both under civil and criminal law in India. Under civil law, a defamation suit can be filed for damages under the Law of Torts. Criminal defamation is addressed under Section 499 and punishable under Section 500 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860. The user can file a civil suit for compensation in the appropriate civil court and simultaneously initiate criminal proceedings by filing a complaint with the magistrate. Ensure evidence of the defamatory statement and its impact is well-documented for both proceedings.

Both offenses are cognizable and bailable offence and triable by a Magistrate. On appeal, bail can be provided by the police officer who has custody of the offender or by the court. To obtain bail, a bail bond needs to be executed, with or without the presence of sureties.   In motor accident cases both the owner and driver of the vehicle are liable to face prosecution proceedings initiated before the Motor Accident Claim Tribunal once an FIR is lodged in the police station in hit and run case and the legal heirs of the deceased victim and the injured persons apply to the Tribunal under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicle Act, 1988 within six months of the occurrence of the accident.  Section 164 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 (as amended in 2019) states that the owner of the motor vehicle or the authorized insurer shall be liable to pay compensation of five lakh rupees in case of death or two and a half lakh rupees in case of grievous hurt to the legal heirs or the victim, as the case may be. The claimant is not required to prove that the death or grievous hurt was due to any wrongful act or neglect of the owner or any other person. In this context, the judgment passed by the Calcutta High Court in the case of Senjuti Roy (Nee Sengupta) VS New India Assurance Co. Ltd. and the judgment passed by the Rajasthan High Court in the case of Ganesh Bairwa VS Ramphool Bairwa may be referred. Given the complexity of the motor accident case as stated in the query that involves delayed registration of the vehicle, driving a vehicle on the road without insurance and other vital documents, absconding of a vehicle in hit and run case, contradictory statements of the witnesses and finally the investigation report of the police, the Tribunal may pass an order for payment of compensation to the claimant against the defaulted parties. Fine as a penalty is imposed only if there is a criminal prosecution. You have to establish the fact before the Court denying that you were not driving the vehicle rashly and that the accident arose not on account of your negligence. You have to take the defense that in spite of cautious driving you met with an accident. Unless you plead guilty generally fine is not imposed. The maximum fine for both offences is around Rs.1500. under Section 279 and 337 IPC if you are ready to plead guilty then the court will impose the fine and close the case but it is better if you can engage the service of an Advocate to navigate the issue in the right way. You may like to contest the case but the court case will drag you for years and you may have to waste your time, energy, and money on litigation as well as lawyer fees which may be ten times the amount that you may pay as a fine, hence better pay the fine amount, which appears to be very minimum and come out of this crisis.

So, on receipt of notice under Sec.25 of PSSA, you should try your best to negotiate the loan with the lender/financier. You can try to negotiate a debt settlement on your own (under OTS- One-time settlement scheme) if your pocket permits, but sometimes it's typically done through third parties like debt relief companies, which you may hire to negotiate the settlement matter with the lender on your behalf. With this method, you will make payments to the debt settlement company rather than your creditors/lenders, along with the payment of fees or service charges. Debt settlement is an agreement between a lender Bank and a borrower in which the borrower repays a portion of a loan balance and the lender forgives the balance. You may consider starting the negotiation by offering to pay 25% or 30% of your outstanding balance in return for forgiveness on the rest. But, it may be noted that while there are legitimate debt relief/settlement companies, there are also many fraud/scam operations. So, if you're considering one, the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau(CFPB) suggests contacting your state Attorney General's(AG) office and local consumer protection agency to ask if they have any consumer complaints pending on file about that company. Some states require that debt settlement companies be licensed, which may provide some added protection. Although a debt settlement can offload some of your financial burden, there are also a few potential risks and downsides to consider. First, a debt settlement will affect your credit score in CIBIL. That will make it more difficult for you to get credit or good interest rates in the future. Another potential drawback is that when you settle debt, you could face tax consequences. Finally, when you settle a debt with a credit card company, your account is closed once the settlement is complete. So you could potentially have no credit facility to use a credit card further owing to your poor credit score. Further, a quick counseling session with a certified credit counselor can help you discover your options and choose the right path forward.

Section 191 of the IPC deals with the filing of false evidence, while section 340 of the Cr. PC outlines the process for making a complaint for this offense. Perjury is defined as the filing of false evidence or a false affidavit before a court knowing that it is false.

answer_ref: Dear Client,Under Section 19 of the Prevention of Corruption Act, 1988, sanction for prosecution is required for an offence punishable under Sections 7, 10, 11, 13, 15 of the Act, while under Section 197(1) Cr. P.C. sanction is required for an offence committed by a public servant while acting or purporting to act in the discharge of his official duty, and not otherwise. After the amendment of the Prevention of Corruption Act, in 2018, it significantly extended the provisions of PCA and gave it the required edge to tackle bribery/corruption involving commercial entities/private companies. According to Section 9 of the amended Act, a commercial organization can be held liable âif any person associated with such commercial organization gives or promises to give any undue advantage to a public servantâ with an intent to obtain or retain business or any advantage for that commercial organization. This provision covers all types of entities (including domestic companies, foreign companies, and partnerships) doing business in India. Thus, while the PCA, 1988 applied to public sector employees, the Act has been amended to encompass situations where private organizations and individuals can also be held accountable for indulging in corrupt practices. Further, the CBI investigates cases of corruption in compliance with the provisions of the Prevention of Corruption Act 1988, under the supervision of the Central Vigilance Commission (CVC). This can include cases of bribery, extortion, and other forms of corruption. The CBI has a special division called the Anti-Corruption Branch (ACB). This branch handles the investigation of corruption-related cases. The CBI can initiate suo moto investigations on the basis of information received from the public, the media, or other sources. CBI lays great emphasis on catching corrupt public servants who demand and take bribes. The process of catching such corrupt public servants red-handed while they demand and take bribes is popularly called the 'trap'. It is not a legal term. A set procedure has been devised in CBI to lay a trap against a corrupt public servant. The evidence collected during the process of trap is placed before the court along with the charge sheet and is quite important in securing the conviction of the public servant charged with corruption. So, given the proposition of relevant laws, you may choose the recourse/steps that suit your grievance most in the prevailing situation, If required, hire an experienced Advocate to navigate the issues in the right way.

Under the Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act, 2005, it is crucial for both parties to be notified properly to ensure fair proceedings.

The user should verify with their lawyer why the notice is unready and ensure that all necessary documents and procedural steps have been completed. It may also be prudent to follow up with the court registry to confirm the status and ensure that no additional information or documentation is required from their side.
